about: Money Check (BRIEF §16): 15 items, the same for everyone, written for a 9-year-old reader. Knowledge items follow Lusardi & Mitchell (2011, 2014); behaviour items are adapted from the OECD/INFE Toolkit (2022); now-or-later choices follow Meier & Sprenger (2010); risk choices simplify Holt & Laury (2002); money beliefs use Klontz Money Script Inventory constructs (Klontz et al. 2011). Inspired by peer-reviewed research. Not a clinical or licensed assessment.

items.prompt: You save 100 baht. Each year the bank adds 10 baht for every 100 baht you have. You leave it all there for 2 years. How much do you have?
items.explain: After year one you have 110 baht. In year two the bank adds 10 baht for every 100, so 11 more: 121 baht. The extra you earn starts earning extra too.

items.prompt: Your money sits in a jar and earns nothing. Shop prices go up by 5 baht for every 100 baht each year. A year later, what can your money buy?
items.explain: The jar still holds the same baht, but things cost more. So the same money buys less. That is inflation.

items.prompt: Which is usually safer for your savings?
options: Putting it all in one company
Spreading it across many different things
items.explain: If one thing goes badly, the others can hold you up. Spreading your money out is called diversification.

items.prompt: Someone will give you 100 baht. They can give it today or next year. Which is worth more to you?
options: They are worth exactly the same
items.explain: Money today can be saved to earn more, and prices may rise by next year. So 100 baht today is worth a little more than 100 baht later.

items.prompt: A message says: “Send 500 baht today and get 5,000 baht next week. Only 10 places left!” What is this most likely?
options: A great way to get rich
A scam that rushes you with a big promise
items.explain: A huge promise plus a rush to decide is how many scams work. Real savings never promise to turn 500 into 5,000 in a week.

items.prompt: When you get money, how often do you keep some of it to save?
Before you buy something, how often do you check that you can really afford it?
How often do you compare prices before you buy?
How often do you keep track of the money you spend?
Which would you pick: 100 baht today, or 120 baht in one month?
And this one: 100 baht in 6 months, or 120 baht in 7 months?
Pick one: 50 baht for sure, or flip a coin. Heads you get 120 baht, tails you get nothing.
Now pick again: 80 baht for sure, or flip a coin. Heads you get 120 baht, tails you get nothing.
Do you agree? “More money would fix all my problems.”
Do you agree? “Expensive things show that a person is important.”

turtle.name: Steady Turtle
turtle.line: You like to wait and play it safe.
strengths: You save steadily and plan ahead.
You rarely panic when prices jump around.
blindSpots: Money kept too safe can lose value as prices rise.
You might skip chances to learn how investing works.
turtle.scam: “Guaranteed” savings schemes that promise high, steady returns with no risk. Real safe returns are small; high returns always come with risk.

eagle.name: Patient Eagle
eagle.line: You can wait, and you’re fine with ups and downs.
strengths: You think about the long run.
Prices going up and down don’t scare you off.
blindSpots: Feeling too sure about one big bet.
Putting too much money in one place.
eagle.scam: “Insider tips” about a coin or stock that will soar. Pump-and-dump groups use them to sell to you at the top.

cat.name: Cosy Cat
cat.line: You enjoy today and avoid risky bets.
strengths: You stay away from risky gambles.
blindSpots: Small spends add up without you noticing.
cat.scam: “Today only!” deals and fake discounts that rush you to pay before you can think.

monkey.name: Spark Monkey
monkey.line: You move fast and love trying new things.
strengths: You’re curious and quick to learn.
You’re brave about trying new ideas.
blindSpots: Chasing hype because everyone else is.
monkey.scam: Get-rich-quick coins and “double your money” offers that pump up hype, then disappear with the money.
